People will probably think I'm exaggerating, but I honestly, genuinely think this is THE best WWII shooter that released to date. It has the PERFECT balance between serious and fun - they really nailed the heavy, depressing atmosphere of the horrors of war, from gore and filth, through scenes of unjust cruelty, to INSANELY well crafted and haunting soundtrack, but you also get your usual Call of Duty "You're the hero of this story, go save the day" action, because games are supposed to be fun, first and foremost. Even the mission briefing cutscenes, which serve as loading screens, are a real treat to watch and do a great job immersing you in the confilct.

I've completed it countless times on console over the years and it still brings me joy to this day. It is a great shame that the stock multiplayer mode no longer works, but you know what? I still much rather recommend (and pay for) this version than the vast majority of games released within the last 5 years. This game is what AAA gaming used to be all about. Plus, they actually bothered to remove the multiplayer tags from the Steam store page, which I can appreciate. You still can (and should) play the multiplayer mode (including the regular thing, zombies AND co-op campaign) through a fan project called Plutonium, which I cannot recommend enough.

If you've never played this game and enjoy shooters, particularly war shooters, PLEASE give this a try. Please. It's well worth it on a 25% discount with the aforementioned Plutonium. And, in case you're familiar with the console version, this one has all the DLCs included from the get go (additional maps for multi and 3 zombie maps), which is pretty neat.
Its cool, go use plutonium for better experience.

10/10. Definitely my favourite WWII CoD. In my opinion it is the exact moment (along the OG MW trilogy and two first Black Ops) when the series peaked. Unlike other WWII CoDs, this one is darker, grittier and showes WWII (especially Eastern Front) not through the idealized lenses of Hollywood.

Soundtrack goes hard (Gary Oldman screaming as Reznov does so too!) and missions themselves are memorable and enjoyable. Furthermore, this is the game where Zombies mode debuted for the first time (and you get all 4 Zombie maps for free) and it is fun to play with your friends. Also, despite its age you can still find people playing this game online on Plutonium and it is fun too. Last, but not least, this game at the Veteran difficulty is the toughest one to beat in the whole series (yup, that's due to grenade swarm).

The only problem is the price. Activision shouldn't make us pay so much for a game released back in 2008. But if you wait until some of Steam's sale you should find it in more normal prize ranges.

And now at the end: GO LOCKE, GRAB THE GAME AND SHOOT THOSE PT BOATS!

# Call of Duty: World at War Review

World at War delivers fast, brutal, and satisfying classic Call of Duty gameplay. The campaign, multiplayer, and Zombies mode provide enough variety to make it one of the strongest entries from the older era of the franchise.

---{ Campaign }---
☐ Forgettable
☐ Average
☐ Good
☑ Excellent
☐ Historical masterpiece

The campaign presents World War II as violent, desperate, and unforgiving instead of making it feel heroic or clean. The American Pacific and Soviet Eastern Front missions create memorable battles with a darker atmosphere than most Call of Duty campaigns.

---{ Zombies }---
☐ Unnecessary
☐ Basic
☐ Good
☐ Very good
☑ Legendary

World at War introduced Nazi Zombies, one of the most important and replayable modes in Call of Duty history. Its simple maps, eerie atmosphere, escalating difficulty, and cooperative gameplay created the foundation for everything that followed.

The multiplayer uses the familiar progression and perk systems from Call of Duty 4 while adding weapons, maps, and vehicles suited to World War II. Some weapons and mechanics are unbalanced, but the core experience remains enjoyable.

The weapons sound powerful, the soundtrack is intense, and the soldiers constantly shouting around you makes every battle feel chaotic. Its grim presentation and disturbing imagery give the game an identity unlike most other Call of Duty titles.

This game is a true masterpiece and has passed the test of time. This game was my first experience to the Call of Duty franchise when my uncle rented this game when I was 8 or 9 years old. The campaign the zombies and the multiplayer all have this eerie vibe to them and a more greyed out look compared to other games. The game just gives you a rough and scary vibe like somewhere you don't want to be. They captured WW2 very well through the campaign. There are many times where you must do things you don't want to do and if you don't do them things can end up worse than if you had done them. I don't want to write any spoilers here as the campaign is excellent and worth a play through. Even for a game from 2008 there are limbs flying off bodies and unlike a traditional Call of Duty game where you mostly fight alone or with 1-2 people as a squad, World at War puts you on a battlefield with tons of others. The campaign is the best campaign for me out of any Call of Duty game followed by the Modern Warfare series. 10/10 Campaign.

Zombies was originally introduced in this Call of Duty for the first time ever and became the popular game mode of the franchise of today. The maps are all very small due to the limited hardware at the time but the developers really went out of their way to make them unique. Nacht der Untoten this is the first ever zombies map it's very tight and compact, there are no perks just a few wall buys and the iconic mystery box. Your stuck all alone in a bunker with hordes of zombies flanking you from all sides with nowhere to run and it captures that perfectly. Playing this map as a kid for the first time really scared me and looking back on it as an adult I really think that the devs did a wonderful job creating this mode and map to give that vibe. You look at the childish current zombies of today and it's not scary at all, it's more like an arcade. 

The second map Verrückt is in my opinion the best zombies map in the game and in terms of location an…

When someone says Call of Duty, this is THE game I think of. It's gritty, it's brutal, it's fun and it gave us so many great things like the Zombies mode. There's also an endless plethora of custom Zombies maps that are a blast to play.

It's worth it if you're really into Zombies, and well worth the entry fee for the stellar campaign. In my top 3 CoD titles for sure.
